items.title: An insular chain of command
items.author: Jake Rogers
items.content: The functional architecture of the human insula is shown to contain four regions, with an anterior polar region exerting direct influence over posterior pain-related regions.

items.title: Glioma modulation of inhibitory neuron signalling
items.author: Darran Yates
items.content: A new study reports that gliomas can regulate the signalling of inhibitory neurons, promoting tumour progression.

items.title: Reappraising emotion regulation
items.author: Jake Rogers
items.content: The assumed link between cognitive reappraisal and activity in regulatory prefrontal circuits in humans is shown to be absent in task-based functional MRI datasets.

items.title: Brain extracellular matrix remodelling in health and neuropsychiatric disorders
items.author: Juan Nacher
items.content: Brain extracellular matrix (ECM) shapes neuronal physiology and function. In this Review, Dityatev and colleagues describe the organization, function and remodelling of the ECM in the healthy brain and consider how altered ECM function may contribute to the pathogenesis of neuropsychiatric disorders.

items.title: Psilocybin reproducibility
items.author: Sian Lewis
items.content: Psilocybin is shown in this study to produce consistent acute behavioural effects but small or absent sustained effects, which could explain the lack of robustness and reproducibility in past studies.

items.title: A pathway to toxic extracellular vesicle secretion
items.author: Katherine Whalley
items.content: The ion channel P2RX7 drives the transition of microglia to an inflammatory state in a mouse model of tauopathy and contributes to pathogenic extracellular vesicle-mediated tau propagation.

items.title: Extracellular vesicles and their role in neurodegenerative diseases
items.author: Andrew F. Hill
items.content: Extracellular vesicles are membrane-bound particles that are involved in intercellular communication in the nervous system. In this Review, Spiers, Broatch and Hill examine the role of these vesicles in the biology, diagnosis and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.

items.title: The many facets of human brain asymmetry
items.author: Clyde Francks
items.content: Contrasting the right and left hemisphere has undergone a methodological and conceptual transformation. In this Review, Francks and colleagues focus on brain asymmetry as a multivariate and multiscale organizational feature of the human brain while discussing its variability across individuals and how left–right asymmetry supports cognition and behaviour.
